body_html:
Solar sodium: 6.264 ± 0.119

Asplund, Amarsi & Grevesse 2021: 6.22 ± 0.03  ·  this measurement +0.044 dex

The three-dimensional non-LTE products apply published line-by-line corrections (Asplund et al. 2021; Canocchi et al. 2026) to our one-dimensional fits; they are not our own three-dimensional calculation. The H- and K-band products sit about 0.4 dex below the visible ones. They are shown as measured, with their full error bars.

Our best HARPS product, chosen the same way as for iron: the Reference Grade analysis with the most complete treatment, then the most lines. HARPS is the instrument we use for the stars that follow, so the Sun is anchored on it. Products and engines are not averaged together.

Line grades

Every product is measured on one of three grades of spectral lines and the grades are never mixed in one number.

GradeWhat it meansThis element
Reference Gradelines from a published solar line set (Asplund et al. 2021 and similar), measured with the oscillator strengths the authors used30 products -- Na I · Asplund et al. 2021 lines
Codex Gradelines chosen by the Codex whose oscillator strength carries a published uncertainty (laboratory measurement, NIST accuracy class A-C, or the paper's own stated error), between 5% and 60% deep54 products -- Na I · Codex-graded lines
Deep Gradethe same oscillator-strength rule on lines deeper than 60% -- stronger lines, more sensitive to damping and the model atmosphere28 products -- Na I · Deep-graded lines

How to read this forest. Each row is one independent product, preserving its band, holding, engine, indicator and line set. Engines and indicator families are never averaged. Solid bars show the supplied statistical uncertainty; wireframes show the supplied systematic uncertainty. The statistical basis and any incomplete error budget remain attached to the row. How this was measured

Every sodium value on this page comes from fitting synthetic spectra to the observed solar spectrum, line by line or band by band, with the sodium abundance as the free parameter. The synthesis includes the atomic lines and the molecular opacity in every window, so blended absorption is modelled rather than attributed to the line being measured. The continuum is placed locally around every line by comparing the observation with the synthesis on its own highest pixels, and ground-based spectra are telluric-corrected across their full range.

Each indicator is measured independently on each solar spectrum and reported separately; nothing is averaged across indicators or instruments. Where a 3D or NLTE correction is published for the lines, it is applied as its own product (1D-LTE, 1D-NLTE and 3D-NLTE are separate rows). Every value carries a full uncertainty budget: fit, line strengths, microturbulence, continuum, fit window, model atmosphere, telluric residual, and the spread between spectra, each measured by refitting with that one input changed. The headline at the top is the Asplund-grade product: a published line set, the most complete treatment, then the most lines.

Solar sodium context

Sodium is traced by neutral Na I lines from the near-ultraviolet to the K band. The reference lines are the five Asplund et al. 2021 used (4751, 5148, 6154, 6160 and 10746 Å), with the oscillator strengths they adopted. Na I departs from LTE, so each spectrum also carries non-LTE products; each set, spectrum and treatment remains a separate product.
